evidence.source: Edith Aldridge, “Neg-to-Q: The Historical Origin and Development of Question Particles in Chinese,” The Linguistic Review 28.4 (2011)
evidence.text: Aldridge proposes the modern Mandarin question particle ma developed from negative existential 無 wu. She cites Tang-dynasty examples attributed to Bai Juyi with sentence-final 無, including 秋寒有酒無 and 今日池邊識我無; she reports that from the ninth century 無 was often written 麼 /mua/ in questions. Her account distinguishes the grammatical history of the particle from the formation of 嗎 and says 嗎 later replaced the question-particle spelling. This is a scholarly proposal, not evidence that the graph 嗎 itself was used in the cited Tang examples.
evidence.title: Neg-to-Q: The historical origin and development of question particles in Chinese

gaps: No primary paleographic sequence for 嗎 was available: the Taiwanese Ministry of Education entry states it is absent from Shuowen and does not expose its ancient-form records in the accessible page. Do not invent an ancient glyph ancestor or report graphic corruption.

The question-particle word history is separate from the graph. Aldridge’s account traces the particle through clause-final 無 and ninth-century 麼, but the research here did not establish when 嗎 itself first represented that particle, nor a complete semantic path from negative existential to question marker.

The Ministry of Education and Han Dian preserve 嗎 as a colloquial/俗 form of 罵. This competing lexical use should not be collapsed into the question particle. The evidence supports a 口-semantic/馬-phonetic account for 嗎-as-罵; it does not independently demonstrate that 馬 supplied the sound of the later particle graph.

No independently established name or pronunciation for any depicted object underlies the particle’s proposed sound borrowing. Aldridge reconstructs the particle’s path from 無 and describes early Mandarin sound change; that is not evidence for a borrowed horse/object name. The 口＋馬 phonetic component account belongs to graphic analysis and is distinct from the whole-word borrowing account.

Current reading records locally inspected: sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt rows 50055–50063 for U+55CE and 45674–45678 for U+5417; pipeline/data/unihan-kmandarin-hsk1.tsv rows 104, 392–393; Baxter–Sagart rows 1898 (口) and 2220 (馬). These local files are not emitted as external evidence because the requested character-specific official Unihan pages could not be verified. Host Mandarin is ma; traditional 馬 and simplified 马 are mǎ. The host reading was not substituted for the 馬 component reading.

No Baxter–Sagart reconstruction for 嗎 was located in the checked local dataset; therefore no historical sound comparison for 馬 → 嗎 can be claimed within that system. 馬 *mˤraʔ and 口 *kʰˤ(r)oʔ are the inspected system entries; do not merge them with other reconstruction systems.
The cited 《西廂記》 question-particle quotation is attributed to 董解元, but the specific text’s date and earliest surviving witness were not established here; the CText text page returned 403 on opening.

No evidence found that 嗎’s older graphic history involved corruption. The dictionary tradition instead describes it as 口＋馬 for the ‘scold’ usage; the later question-particle use may reflect character choice/borrowing in a written tradition, but the exact graphic chronology remains unresolved.
No verified reuse or bulk-extraction terms were found for recurring sources; no local extract is recommended on this evidence.

No primary paleographic sequence for 嗎 or 吗 was established. The Ministry of Education entry says 嗎 is absent from Shuowen and its accessible form table has no published ancient-form records; no corruption claim is supported.

The graphic analysis 口 (semantic) + 馬 (phonetic) is specifically supported for the older 嗎-as-罵 lexical use. Evidence examined does not establish that this component analysis explains the graph’s later question-particle use.

The question particle’s earliest surviving use and its semantic transition from negative existential 無 through forms such as 麼 remain outside this run’s inspected primary evidence. The literary quotation cited by the Ministry of Education is undated on that page.

Official Unihan character-specific endpoints failed in this run, and a current pronunciation comparison for 吗/嗎 versus 马/馬 could not be independently verified here. Historical pronunciation evidence from a component cannot be transferred to the host.

No usable glyph image candidate was located with verified identity, direct image URL, and provenance. Since the graphic history of 嗎 itself is undocumented in the inspected sources, no image is proposed.
